units.title: Unit 33 — Studying English and taking exams
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 72–73 (PDF pages 73–74).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
units.category: Language-learning progress, exam preparation and results
learningObjectives: Describe vocabulary range, pronunciation, accuracy, fluency and other language-learning strengths and difficulties.
Use natural combinations such as make progress, make yourself understood, pick things up and have a good ear for language.
Distinguish adjectives from adverbs when describing a speaker and the way someone speaks.
Talk about exam preparation, candidates, essays, grades and exam results using take/do, pass, fail and retake.
Describe learning goals using work on, increase vocabulary, get through and do your best.

items.example: How are you getting on with your English course?
items.note: Here get on refers to the progress a learner is making.

items.example: Reading varied texts can help you develop a wide vocabulary.
items.note: Know and be able to use many different words; contrast with a basic vocabulary.

items.example: My vocabulary has improved since I started reading in English.
items.note: The words known or used by a person or in a language.

items.example: Her answers are usually accurate.
items.note: Adjective describing something that is correct; compare the adverb accurately.

items.example: He can describe the problem accurately in English.
items.note: Adverb modifying a verb; say speaks accurately, not speaks accurate.

items.example: She's a fluent speaker, although she sometimes makes mistakes.
items.note: Adjective for speaking a language naturally and without frequent pauses.

items.example: He speaks French fluently after years of practice.
items.note: Adverb describing how somebody speaks; compare a fluent speaker.

items.example: She became a fluent speaker after living abroad.
items.note: Fluent is an adjective used before the noun speaker.

items.pt: falar com precisão; falar sem erros
items.example: Try to speak accurately without stopping after every word.
items.note: Accurately is an adverb modifying speak; fluency and accuracy are separate strengths.

items.example: He has a noticeable accent, but everyone understands him.
items.note: The way someone pronounces words; an accent does not necessarily prevent understanding.

items.example: My colleague has a strong accent, but his explanations are clear.
items.note: Strong is a common adjective used to describe a noticeable accent.

items.example: Could you pronounce the final word again?
items.note: A verb for saying the sounds of a word.

items.example: The word stop begins with two consonants.
items.note: A speech sound represented by a letter other than a, e, i, o or u in the simple alphabet exercise.

items.example: The letter e is a vowel in English.
items.note: The alphabet letters a, e, i, o and u are commonly called vowels; vowel sounds are a separate pronunciation concept.

items.example: We practised spelling names using the English alphabet.
items.note: The set of letters used to write a language.

items.example: Even with limited vocabulary, she can make herself understood.
items.note: Communicate clearly enough for others to understand your meaning.

items.example: Listening to podcasts can increase your vocabulary.
items.note: Increase means make larger; expand your range of known words.

items.example: The first lessons teach basic sentence patterns.
items.note: Simple or elementary; a basic vocabulary has relatively few words.

items.example: I'm willing to practise speaking with a new partner.
items.note: Willing to means happy and ready to do something, not merely able to do it.

items.pt: experimentar o uso da língua; testar formas de expressão
items.example: Don't be afraid to experiment with language in your writing.
items.note: Try new words or structures and see how they work.

items.example: I got the last answer wrong but understood the correction.
items.note: A common pattern for answering or doing something incorrectly.

items.example: Everyone makes a mistake occasionally when learning a language.
items.note: Use make a mistake, not do a mistake.

items.example: She learns from her mistakes and rarely repeats them.
items.note: Use feedback from errors to improve performance.

items.example: After two months of practice, we're making progress.
items.note: Progress is uncountable in this general sense; do not normally say a progress.

items.pt: aprender algo com facilidade; assimilar rapidamente
items.example: She picked up several useful expressions from the film.
items.note: Here pick up means learn without much formal effort; not lift an object.

items.word: have a good ear for language
items.example: He has a good ear for language and copies new sounds well.
items.note: Be good at hearing, distinguishing and repeating the sounds of a language.

items.example: She speaks English well in technical meetings.
items.note: Well is the adverb after speak; not speak English good.

items.pt: fazer uma prova; prestar um exame
items.example: I'm going to take an exam at the end of the course.
items.note: Use take or do an exam, not make an exam.

items.pt: fazer uma prova; realizar um exame
items.example: The class will do an exam in June.
items.note: An alternative to take an exam; make an exam is incorrect for sitting a test.

items.pt: passar numa prova; ser aprovado em exame
items.example: He passed the exam on his first attempt.
items.note: Obtain a successful result; opposite: fail an exam.

items.pt: reprovar em uma prova; não passar no exame
items.example: She failed the exam but can take it again next term.
items.note: Not achieve the result needed to pass; do not say lose an exam.

items.pt: revisar a matéria para uma prova
items.example: I revise for exams by testing myself with flashcards.
items.note: British English for studying material again before a test.

items.pt: refazer uma prova; prestar o exame novamente
items.example: You can retake the exam if your first result is too low.
items.note: Take an examination another time, often after failing.

items.example: Preparing for three exams at once is hard work.
items.note: Work requiring considerable time or effort.

items.pt: dar o melhor de si; esforçar-se ao máximo
items.example: Do your best, even if you find the questions difficult.
items.note: Make as much effort as possible; do not say make your best.

items.example: With a bit of luck, I'll finish my revision before Friday.
items.note: An informal expression of hope that things will go well.

items.example: Every candidate must bring identification to the exam.
items.note: In this context, someone taking an examination.

items.pt: candidato bem preparado; candidato com boas chances
items.example: She is a strong candidate for the advanced language exam.
items.note: A learner considered likely to perform well.

items.example: She received an excellent grade for her presentation.
items.note: A level or score awarded for schoolwork or an exam; often called a mark in British English.

items.example: He got a high mark in his listening test.
items.note: British English noun for a test score; often close in meaning to grade.

items.example: She worked carefully and got a good grade.
items.note: Get is a natural verb with grades and marks.

items.example: I hope you do well in your speaking exam.
items.note: Succeed or achieve a good result; opposite do badly.

items.example: He did badly in the first test but improved later.
items.note: Get a poor result; opposite do well.

items.example: We hope to get through the coursebook before the holiday.
items.note: Here get through means finish studying the material; not survive an experience.

items.example: Our coursebook contains several listening exercises.
items.note: A book designed for a particular course.

items.example: Regular revision made the final test easier.
items.note: British English noun related to revise.

items.pt: preparação para provas; preparação para exames
items.example: Exam preparation should include timed practice.
items.note: Getting ready for an exam through study and practice.

items.pt: escrever uma redação; redigir um ensaio
items.example: They have to write an essay about education.
items.note: Do an essay and write an essay are both possible here.

items.example: My essay gives two reasons for learning another language.
items.note: A short written text discussing a particular subject.

items.pt: trabalhar em algo; dedicar-se a melhorar algo
items.example: I need to work on my pronunciation before the test.
items.note: Spend time trying to improve or finish something.

sectionsChecked: A: How are they getting on?; learner descriptions, numbered glosses and common mistakes
B: Examinations; language-help contrast, coursebook narrative and numbered glosses

units.title: Unit 34 — University education
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 74–75 (PDF pages 75–76).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
units.category: University subjects, degrees and academic pathways
learningObjectives: Name university subjects and connect them to related professions.
Describe university entry, qualifications, degree courses, grades and certificates.
Use academic terminology for lecturers, lectures, laboratories, arts and science courses.
Distinguish undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate stages, including Master’s and PhD degrees.

items.example: She plans to study medicine after leaving school.
items.note: In this context medicine is a university subject for becoming a doctor, not a substance you take.

items.example: Her goal is to work as a doctor in a small town.
items.note: The profession connected with studying medicine in the source.

items.example: He is studying engineering at university.
items.note: A university subject connected with the profession engineer.

items.example: An engineer helped design the new bridge.
items.note: The profession linked to engineering.

items.example: She chose economics because she enjoys analysing markets.
items.note: A subject that examines economic activity; different from economy.

items.example: The economist explained why food prices had risen.
items.note: A professional who studies or works in economics.

items.example: We studied accounting as part of business studies.
items.note: An academic subject dealing with how businesses operate.

items.pt: entrar no mundo dos negócios; começar a atuar no setor empresarial
items.example: After graduating, she decided to go into business.
items.note: Start working in commercial activity, sometimes by running a company.

items.example: She studies law and wants to work in legal services.
items.note: Here law is the university subject connected with lawyers.

items.example: The lawyer gave the family some useful advice.
items.note: A professional who works with legal matters; the profession linked to law.

items.example: He chose architecture because he enjoys designing buildings.
items.note: A subject related to planning and designing buildings.

items.example: An architect designed the new library.
items.note: The profession linked to architecture.

items.example: She's taking an introductory course in psychology.
items.note: The academic study of the mind and behaviour.

items.example: The psychologist spoke about how people learn.
items.note: The profession linked to studying psychology.

items.pt: estudar uma disciplina; cursar uma área de conhecimento
items.example: You can study several subjects in your first year.
items.note: Do or study a subject are both possible in this context.

items.example: This qualification may help her apply for a better job.
items.note: Official evidence of completing a course or passing a required examination.

items.example: He hopes to qualify as a teacher next year.
items.note: Verb corresponding to qualification and qualified.

items.example: She is a qualified nurse with several years of experience.
items.note: Adjective meaning trained or officially qualified for a job.

items.example: He revised every evening before his final school exams.
items.note: School-leaving examinations can affect university admission in the system described.

items.example: She got good grades and applied for a competitive course.
items.note: Get good grades is a natural expression for good academic results.

items.example: He got a place at university after passing his final exams.
items.note: Be offered admission; in Britain entry requirements vary by institution.

items.example: She received her degree after completing the course.
items.note: A university qualification; different from a degree of temperature.

items.pt: fazer uma graduação; cursar uma formação universitária
items.example: He's doing a degree in engineering.
items.note: Common British English pattern for studying a university degree.

items.pt: estudar para obter um diploma universitário
items.example: She's studying for a degree in economics.
items.note: An alternative to do a degree.

items.example: She got her degree in psychology last summer.
items.note: Successfully complete the course and obtain the qualification.

items.pt: curso de graduação; curso superior que concede grau
items.example: Some degree courses require practical work.
items.note: A course of study leading to a university degree.

items.example: He framed the certificate he received at graduation.
items.note: A document proving successful completion of a course or award.

items.example: This course lasts two years.
items.note: Here last describes duration, not the adjective meaning final.

items.pt: professor universitário; docente que ministra aulas expositivas
items.example: Our lecturer explained the main ideas clearly.
items.note: A common title for a university teacher in the UK; not identical to the universal term professor.

items.example: We attended a lecture on renewable energy.
items.note: A university teaching session in which a teacher speaks to a group.

items.pt: professor titular; professor universitário sênior (título britânico)
items.example: The professor led a research group at the university.
items.note: In the UK this is generally a senior academic title, not a title for every university teacher.

items.example: History and literature are examples of arts subjects.
items.note: Here arts covers humanities subjects, not only creative arts.

items.example: He is doing a science degree with practical classes.
items.note: In this textbook, science degrees often include time in laboratories.

items.example: I spent the afternoon reading in the university library.
items.note: Place with books and study resources, illustrated in the unit.

items.example: The students tested their samples in the laboratory.
items.note: A place where scientific experiments or practical work take place.

items.example: Our lab has equipment for basic chemistry experiments.
items.note: Informal shortened form of laboratory.

items.pt: escrever uma redação; produzir um ensaio
items.example: We had to write an essay about a historical event.
items.note: Typical assignment in many arts subjects; also studied in Unit 33.

items.example: Completing the course was a major success for her.
items.note: Noun related to succeed and successful.

items.pt: conseguir fazer algo; ter êxito em algo
items.example: She succeeded in finishing her thesis early.
items.note: Succeed in + -ing form; not succeed to finish in this meaning.

items.example: The course was successful and attracted many applicants.
items.note: Adjective corresponding to success; opposite unsuccessful.

items.example: His first application was unsuccessful, so he tried again.
items.note: Negative adjective formed with un-; it does not mean the person is incapable.

items.example: As an undergraduate, she studied physics and maths.
items.note: A student working towards a first university degree.

items.example: The programme welcomes graduates from several disciplines.
items.note: Noun: a person who has completed a university degree; compare undergraduate.

items.pt: passar a fazer algo posteriormente; prosseguir para outra etapa
items.example: After her degree, she went on to study for a Master's.
items.note: Describe the next stage in someone's education or career.

items.example: He completed a Master's degree before applying for a PhD.
items.note: A postgraduate qualification typically taken after a first degree.

items.pt: mestrado em artes ou humanidades (Master of Arts)
items.example: She completed an MA in history.
items.note: Abbreviation for Master of Arts; a type of Master's degree.

items.example: He's doing an MSc in computer science.
items.note: Abbreviation for Master of Science; note the article an.

items.pt: pós-graduação stricto sensu; grau acadêmico posterior à graduação
items.example: A Master's is one type of postgraduate degree.
items.note: A university degree studied after completing a first degree.

items.pt: doutorado; título de doutor (Doctor of Philosophy)
items.example: She began a PhD in chemistry after her Master's.
items.note: A research doctorate; despite the name, it is awarded in many subjects.

items.example: His research focuses on new battery materials.
items.note: Detailed study designed to increase knowledge of a subject; generally uncountable.

items.example: The students do research on renewable energy.
items.note: Use do research, not make a research.

C: Postgraduate degrees; undergraduate, graduate, Master’s and PhD terminology
